name: Twitch Chat Plinko
description: Type !drop in chat, or the word your streamer picked, and a ball with your name on it drops through a Plinko board on stream. Every drop plays in the order chat sent it, one ball per chatter at a time, bouncing off every peg into a slot worth 5 in the middle and 1000 at the rare edges. Read straight from Twitch chat with nothing to connect and no bot to add.
changelog: Initial release. The sixth product, and the first with its own physics: a board the overlay draws, fed by chat.
obs_hint: Make the browser source your whole canvas, 1920 by 1080. It is a full scene, made for BRB and downtime.
ready_message: Every !drop in your chat drops a ball. Type it in your own chat to see the first one land.
highlights: Chat types !drop, or any word you pick, and a ball with their name on it bounces down a Plinko board on your stream.
Played in the order chat sends it, one ball each. A big chat waits in a line you can see.
Nothing to connect and no bot to add. Top scores fill in as the balls land.

pitch.meta_title: Twitch Chat Plinko - a Plinko game your chat plays
pitch.meta_description: It's Plinko, and now it lives on your Twitch stream. Your chat types one command and their name bounces down the board. Free, one click, no bot.
pitch.tagline: It's Plinko. You know it already. Now it lives on your stream.
pitch.lede: Drop a ball, watch it bounce off the pegs, hope for the edge. Same game, except your Twitch chat is playing: every `!drop` (or the word you pick) sends a ball with that chatter's name on it down the board, and the best scores go up beside it.

pitch.reasons_heading: The Plinko you know, played by your chat.

reasons.title: Played in chat order
reasons.body: Every drop takes its turn in the order chat sent it. When chat is busy, everyone waits in a line that shows on screen.

reasons.title: Scores on screen
reasons.body: The six latest drops and the five best totals fill in beside the board as the balls land.

reasons.title: Nothing to set up
reasons.body: No bot and no account to connect. It reads your Twitch chat directly, like any viewer does.

reasons.title: Follows your mods
reasons.body: When a mod deletes a drop or times someone out, their ball leaves the board. Chatters you have hidden never get one.

pitch.setup_note: Size the browser source to your whole canvas, 1920 by 1080. It is a full scene, made for BRB and downtime.

faq.a: `!drop`, unless you picked another word. Anything after it still counts, so `!drop come on edges` drops a ball too.

faq.q: What if my whole chat drops at once?
faq.a: Everyone gets a turn. Up to 150 balls are on the board at once and ten new ones join every second. Everyone else waits in line in the order they typed, and the line shows on screen.

faq.q: Can one chatter flood the board?
faq.a: No. Each chatter has one ball at a time. Another drop while theirs is still on the board is ignored.
They count from when the overlay loaded. Reloading the browser source starts a new game.

faq.q: My channel already uses !drop. Can I change it?
faq.a: Yes. Pick any word on the Plinko page in your settings, under Integrations, and the board listens for that instead.

faq.q: Does it need the Overlabels bot?
faq.a: No. It reads your chat directly. The bot never has to be in your channel.

pitch.closing: Let your chat drop the first ball tonight.

notes: Hiding commands in the chat feed does not stop Plinko, since that setting only hides them from the feed. Chatters on your hidden list never get a ball.
Scores count from when the overlay loaded. Reloading the browser source starts a new game.
The command is !drop unless you pick another word on the Plinko page (Settings, Integrations). Reload the browser source in OBS after changing it.
